updates.title: Fall Town Meeting opens tonight: what's on the floor
updates.body:
Winchester's Fall Town Meeting begins tonight, Nov. 5, at 7 p.m. More sessions are scheduled for Nov. 9 and Nov. 12, with Nov. 16 held in reserve. The 192 elected members from eight precincts will work through a 45-article warrant, and they need 100 members for a quorum. Philip Frattaroli is the moderator.

WHAT'S ON THE WARRANT
Most of the 45 articles are about money, and most of those are routine:

• Spending and capital (about 20 articles). Articles 10–15 are the capital requests, worth about $4.8 million in the Capital Planning Committee's presentation figures:
  – a $1.1 million fire engine and other vehicles ($1.73 million in total)
  – $900,000 for walkways and stairs at Lincoln School
  – $840,000 for a columbarium and water facility repairs
  – $720,000 for roads and sidewalks
  – HVAC and field design work
Other money articles include FY27 budget adjustments, water/sewer and recreation financing, and free cash transfers to reserves: $350,000 to retiree benefits, $148,000 to health insurance and $400,000 to special education.
• Community Preservation (Article 25). $920,500 for eight projects, led by $400,000 for the Packer-Ellis design and $300,000 for the Leonard pavilion.
• Zoning and land (about 13 articles). These include three Planning Board zoning cleanups, four citizen rezoning or land petitions, an MBTA parcel conveyance, Waterfield easements and a 16-acre conservation deed at Vale.
• Bylaws and local rules. Changes include higher dog license fees, a tougher sidewalk snow-removal bylaw with larger fines, water and sewer liens, a school bus revolving fund, and a reorganized Committee on Names.
• Procedural and housekeeping. Reports, attendance rules and committees.

THE ARTICLES TO WATCH
• Forest Ridge eminent domain (Article 26). The town would take about 13.4 acres for conservation, with an appraisal ceiling of $2.85 million. Grants could lower the net cost, but none are confirmed. The Select Board put off its recommendation until tonight.
• Citizen petitions (Articles 39–43). Five petitions cover two rezonings at 114 Church St. and 18 Raymond Place, a two-part request to free land at the Ledges for a single home, and a call for separate ballot votes on future overrides. The Church Street petitioner has told the Select Board they won't pursue the article this fall.
• Sanborn Carriage House study (Article 30). This $50,000 study is the only article the Select Board has recommended against, by a 4-0 vote.
• Special education reserve (Article 29). The $400,000 request won Select Board support 3-1. The dissenting member favored $200,000.
• Unfinished business. As of the draft motions, the FY27 tax levy reduction (Article 44) and the budget and permitting software request (Article 33) had no dollar amounts.

WHERE THINGS STAND
The Select Board has recommended 18 articles favorably and one unfavorably. It has not recommended the other 26, including several it discussed without voting. No Finance Committee recommendations had been confirmed. The draft motions still contain dollar errors and blank amounts. All 45 results are pending, and we'll update them here as votes come in.
